extracted.intended_audience: philosophers of biology, evolutionary biologists, and advanced students interested in foundations of evolutionary theory
extracted.subtask_description: Criteria and standards for judging competing accounts of how complex organs (e.g., the eye) arise — comparing accidental variation + selection, sudden variation, external (physical/chemical) causes, neo-Lamarckism, and hybrid hypotheses. Focus is on explanatory power with respect to convergence, coordination, heredity, ontogeny, and causality.

rubrics_metrics.name: Account for parallel/convergent development on independent lines
rubrics_metrics.description: Can the theory explain the likeness of structure of the eye (or other complex organs) in species that have not the same history, i.e., parallel development on independent lines of evolution?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The text emphasizes that 'parallel development of the same complex structures on independent lines of evolution' is not plausibly due to mere accumulation of accidental variations. A satisfactory theory must explain how the same complex organ can appear independently (mollusc and vertebrate eyes) without invoking repeated miraculous coincidences of accidental change. Examples and argument: improbability of identical small variations occurring in the same order in separate lineages; ontogenetic/regeneration evidence showing same effect from different processes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Explain preservation and accumulation of infinitesimal variations
rubrics_metrics.description: If variations are 'insensible' (infinitesimal and accidental), the theory must show how they can be preserved and accumulated in the same order across individuals and lineages.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Bergson argues selection alone cannot be appealed to to preserve an incalculable number of infinitesimal changes in the same order; otherwise one must invoke a 'good genius' of the future species. The theory must address how small, individually neutral or non-useful changes become fixed and accumulated coherently.

rubrics_metrics.name: Account for coordination of simultaneous large (sudden) variations
rubrics_metrics.description: If variation occurs by sudden, relatively large leaps, the theory must explain how all parts changed together remain so well coordinated that the organ continues to function.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sudden change of a single part can render an organ non-functional unless all parts change together in complementary fashion. The theory should explain the origin of such coordinated, complementary simultaneous changes rather than assuming chance will produce them in precisely the right combination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Distinguish and justify senses of 'correlation' (solidary vs complementary)
rubrics_metrics.description: The theory must distinguish between 'solidary' correlations (co-occurring changes due to common origin or lesion) and 'complementary' correlations (coordinated changes that maintain or improve function), and must use the correct sense when invoking correlation in explanations of detail.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Bergson illustrates solidary changes with white cats/blue eyes (deafness) and hairless dogs (imperfect dentition) — these are lesions or common-origin effects, not coordinated additions. Using 'correlation' to explain complementary coordinated improvements (e.g., all parts of the eye improving together) is illegitimate unless the theory can justify that form of correlation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clarify the nature of adaptation: passive 'imprint' vs active problem-solving
rubrics_metrics.description: Does the theory treat adaptation as passive imprinting of external forces on matter, or as active organic response and problem-solving (organism appropriating circumstances)?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The text distinguishes a photograph-like 'imprint' (passive) from an apparatus that 'uses' and 'solves' (active). A credible account must not conflate these senses; it must show whether and how passive physico-chemical effects can be transformed into organized active mechanisms that exploit stimuli (e.g., light → retina → nervous-motor integration).

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide a genuine causal mechanism (impelling vs releasing vs unwinding)
rubrics_metrics.description: The theory should specify what kind of cause is invoked — impelling (quantity/quality of cause determines effect), releasing (triggering an invariable effect), or unwinding (releasing a pre-formed effect) — and whether that suffices to explain the observed variations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Bergson warns that many appeals to 'cause' in transformation experiments sit between 'unwinding' and 'releasing' rather than the explanatory 'impelling' sense. A mechanistic explanation must show proportional, explanatory causation of quality/quantity, not merely occasioning or revealing pre-existing patterns.

rubrics_metrics.name: Demonstrate physico-chemical sufficiency across different material substrates
rubrics_metrics.description: If the account invokes direct physical/chemical action of the environment (e.g., light) to produce structures, it must show how such physico-chemistry can produce similar complex organs in organisms with different embryological/chemical substrates (e.g., mollusc egg vs vertebrate egg).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The text questions whether identical organs (eye) could arise under the same external influence when the underlying material (egg chemistry, embryological origins) differs greatly. A successful theory must address this obstacle to a purely external-physical explanation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Be compatible with ontogenetic and regeneration evidence
rubrics_metrics.description: The theory must account for embryological observations and regeneration facts showing identical structures arising via different developmental routes (heteroblastia, regeneration of lens from different tissues).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: vertebrate retina arises from brain expansion; mollusc retina arises directly from ectoderm; in Triton and Salamandra lens regeneration occurs from iris or retinal layers. The theory must explain how same effects result from differing embryogenic causes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Explain the empirical status of transmissibility of acquired characters
rubrics_metrics.description: The theory must confront experimental evidence regarding whether acquired habits/characters are transmissible and clarify whether heredity typically transmits 'deviation' or 'character'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Bergson surveys experiments (Brown-Séquard, Charrin, etc.) and concludes transmissibility of acquired characters is exceptional and ambiguous; when soma influences germ-plasm it may produce general alterations that yield varied outcomes in descendants (inheritance of deviation, not reproduction of the acquired character). A plausible theory must align with this empirical profile or provide decisive experiments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Differentiate between inheritance of deviation and inheritance of character
rubrics_metrics.description: Does heredity reproduce the specific acquired character of the parent, or only a general deviation in the germ-plasm that may manifest differently in offspring?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The text formalizes this distinction: a chemical change C in plasm may cause assorted effects in descendants; often what is inherited is deviation (a tendency to differ), not the precise character acquired. Theorists must account for this when invoking heredity to build complex organs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Handle differences between plant and animal cases
rubrics_metrics.description: A satisfactory evolutionary account must respect that function is less tightly linked to form in plants than in animals, so mechanisms valid for animals may not transfer to plants.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Bergson notes that experimental support for sudden-variation theories is strongest in botany where morphological changes often do not affect function; the theory must therefore distinguish its domain of applicability and explain differing constraints for plants vs animals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid equivocation of key terms ('adaptation', 'correlation')
rubrics_metrics.description: The theory must use central terms consistently and avoid switching senses between premises and conclusions (which leads to paralogism).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Bergson emphasizes careful distinction of senses: passing unconsciously from passive to active 'adaptation' or from solidary to complementary 'correlation' invalidates arguments. Conceptual clarity is required as part of a rigorous explanatory standard.

rubrics_metrics.name: Integrate partial truths of competing theories without overclaiming precision
rubrics_metrics.description: While each current form of evolutionism (neo-Darwinism, sudden-variation, neo-Lamarckism) contributes validly to aspects of evolution, a comprehensive philosophical account must transcend them and indicate where their partial views converge, without pretending to the same scientific precision required for focused empirical research.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Bergson concedes that 'each of them...must be true in its way' and suggests a philosophical synthesis should indicate the positive contribution of each and the point(s) of convergence. The requirement is methodological humility: restrict claims to suitable points of view and avoid overextending mechanisms beyond their evidential support.

rubrics_metrics.name: Account for determinate periods and directions of mutation (mutation theory)
rubrics_metrics.description: If invoking mutation theory (De Vries), the account should explain whether periods of mutation and tendencies to change are determinate and whether directionality of mutation can be admitted (especially in animals).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Bergson notes that mutation theory modifies Darwinism by positing periods where an entire species is 'beset with a tendency to change' and suggests that neo-Darwinians may admit determinate periods and directions of mutation. A satisfactory theory must engage with empirical scope and limits of such claims (e.g., De Vries' verification limited to Oenothera).
